layers.name: quake
layers.desc: Earthquake level 0-5 (user scale of the max plausible intensity)

layers.name: tsunamiH
layers.desc: Max recorded run-up within 75 km, metres x2 (capped 127.5 m)

layers.name: slope
layers.desc: Mean terrain gradient of land, m/km (~5 km relief, heights clamped at sea level)

scales.quake: level 1 = intensity 2–4, 2 = 4–6, 3 = 6–8, 4 = 8–10, 5 = >10 (MMI/MSK-64 points; bins [lo, hi) except 4 = [8, 10] and 5 = I > 10, as the scale says)
scales.tsunami: Soloviev–Imamura intensity I = log2(√2·H): level 1 = I<1 (H<1.4 m), 2 = 1–2 (<2.8 m), 3 = 2–3 (<5.7 m), 4 = 3–4 (<11.3 m), 5 = I≥4
scales.volcano: by distance to Holocene volcanoes and their max VEI: ≤30 km / ≤100 km / ≤300 km / ≤1000 km bands (see method)
scales.landslide: slope class 1–5 (gradient thresholds 8/18/32/55/85 m/km) × trigger factor (0.45 + 0.35·wet + 0.25·min(1, quake/4))

method.quake: For every catalogued epicentre (NCEI significant 2150 BC–present + USGS M>=6 1900–present, merged): intensity at each cell centre by the Allen, Wald & Worden (2012) hypocentral IPE for active crustal regions (J. Seismol. 16:409–433), with distance measured to the nearest point of a rupture of length L(M) from Wells & Coppersmith (1994, subsurface rupture length), an anelastic far-field term −0.0012·(R − 300 km) beyond 300 km (model assumption, form as in Atkinson & Wald 2007), and reduced by 30 km for cell size/location uncertainty; when NCEI reports a higher epicentral intensity the excess is added near the source and tapered as 25/(25+r) with rupture distance r. Magnitudes of pre-instrumental events without one are estimated from I0: the median M of NCEI events of the same country with the same I0 and a known magnitude (depth <= 40 km, at least 5 events), otherwise Shebalin (1968): I0 = 1.5M − 3.5·lg h + 3 (capped at M 7.5). Events without magnitude and intensity are assumed I0 = 7; NCEI intensity XII entries without magnitude or any recorded impact are treated as unknown size. Cell value = max over all events ("max plausible intensity").
method.tsunami: Coastal cells only. Run-ups (NCEI, non-doubtful): level of the run-up height within 75 km, minus 1 within 200 km, minus 2 within 400 km. Source events with max water height: full level within 50 km, minus 1 within 150 km. Shallow (<=70 km) offshore M>=7.5 epicentres: at least level 2 (3 for M>=8.5) within 150·2^(M−7.5) km.
method.volcano: For each GVP Holocene volcano with max Holocene VEI v (unknown -> treated as VEI 1): ≤30 km: 5 if v≥4, 4 if v≥2, else 3; ≤100 km: 4 if v≥5, 3 if v≥3, else 2; ≤300 km: 3 if v≥6, 2 if v≥4, 1 if v≥2; ≤1000 km: 2 if v≥7, 1 if v≥6. Minus 1 for volcanoes without eruptions since 5000 BC. Distance bands after the 10/30/100 km Volcano Population Exposure Index radii (Brown et al. 2015) extended for far-field tephra.
method.landslide: Mean gradient of the ~5 km map relief (public/assets/map/height, clamped at sea level so that coastal bathymetry does not count) on land in each cell -> slope class; trigger factor from the earthquake level and a wetness proxy (vegetation greenness of the NASA Blue Marble June composite; replace with climate precipitation when available, see scheduler option annualPrecip).
